q: What is the concrete size overhead of Brakerski-Yuen's Clifford-only QGC as a function of circuit depth d and wire count w? Asymptotic bounds are given (double-exponential in d IT / polynomial with QPRGs) but the hidden constants are unspecified.
basis: Our toy replication used only a handful of EPR pairs per gate at zero blow-up; extrapolating to real circuits requires a tight constant.
next_steps: Build a small-instance simulator that emits the explicit garbling and counts (EPR pairs, classical bits, gates) as a function of depth 1..6 on random Clifford circuits of width 1..4; fit a scaling model and publish the constant.

q: How does the Clifford-slice Pauli-frame propagation degrade under realistic noise? Our numerical fidelities were 1.0 to machine precision on an ideal simulator.
basis: Real QGC deployment will inherit teleportation's sensitivity to depolarizing/dephasing noise on the EPR resource; the paper is noise-free by construction.
next_steps: Add a depolarizing channel of strength p to each EPR pair in qgc_clifford_teleport.py, sweep p in [1e-4, 1e-1], measure decoded fidelity vs p, and compare to a fault-tolerant Steane-teleportation baseline.

q: Can the double-exponential-in-depth blow-up of the information-theoretic variant be replaced by a double-exponential-in-T-count blow-up?
basis: Our Clifford slice had no blow-up; empirically the cost seems localized to non-Clifford gates. A T-count-parametrized bound would be much more useful than a depth-parametrized one.
next_steps: Extend the code to a single T gate via the magic-state gadget from Section 5, measure encoding size for circuits with T-count 0..3 and depth 4, and check whether the blow-up scales with T-count rather than depth.

q: What is the minimal quantum-secure PRG family sufficient for the computational-security variant of QGC, and does a lattice-based candidate (SIS/LWE) yield practical parameters at lambda=128?
basis: The paper invokes QPRGs abstractly; there is no concrete instantiation with a parameter estimate.
next_steps: Instantiate f_corr with a lattice-based QPRG candidate (e.g., learning-with-rounding); build a security-parameter -> encoding-size table for circuits up to 10^3 gates.

q: Does the constant-depth QNC^0_f encoder property lift into the Sigma-protocol for QMA, giving a QMA protocol whose prover runs in QNC^0 (a strictly stronger complexity statement)?
basis: The paper's Sigma-protocol uses QGC as a black box; the encoder's constant-depth property is not obviously inherited by the protocol.
next_steps: Formalize the Sigma-protocol prover circuit explicitly, count its depth as a function of QGC's encoder depth, and check whether it collapses to constant-depth when fan-out is available.
